chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the two days after the breaking of the fast (Eid al-Fitr): are they fasted or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike for you that you fast them.'

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike (indicating recommended prohibition or karahah)
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: The breaking of the fast, referring to Eid al-Fitr

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the two days after Eid al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the status of the two days immediately following Eid al-Fitr, distinguishing them from the days of Tashreeq (11th–13th Dhu al-Hijjah) which are primarily associated with Eid al-Adha. The Imam’s expression of *karahat* (dislike) indicates a recommended prohibition (*karahat tanzih*), suggesting that while fasting is not invalid, it is discouraged to preserve the joyous spirit of the post-Eid period. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing acts of worship with the celebration of divine blessings.
